archetypes.name: call-site-parity
archetypes.rationale: The allow-list swap of claude-phase3-aggregator for claude-phase3-structure and claude-phase3-plan-fidelity requires verifying those exact kinds are actually emitted by dispatch-with-waterfall.sh — a cross-file traceability risk the static reviewers won't specifically chase.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine scripts/dispatch-with-waterfall.sh to verify the slot_names array and the dynamic kind construction pattern actually produce claude-phase3-structure and claude-phase3-plan-fidelity as emitted strings. Confirm that no previously-listed allow-list kind (including claude-phase3-aggregator, which was removed) is still emitted by any caller in skills/ or scripts/. Also verify that skills/implement/scripts/generate-code-flow-diagram.sh emits exactly implement-code-flow as its --timing-task-kind argument. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: format-compat
archetypes.rationale: The terse and summary output format gained a new claude=N field, changing a documented and operator-visible interface; downstream shell consumers (skills, CI scripts) that parse or compare this output could silently break.
archetypes.prompt_body: Search skills/ and scripts/ for any code that reads, greps, or string-matches against the terse or summary output format (patterns like vendor-tasks=, codex=, cursor=, elapsed=). For each match, determine whether the new claude=N field appended to the parenthetical would cause a parsing failure, a missed match, or a silent wrong result. Also check whether any CI scripts or Makefile targets capture and compare timing-report.sh output against a hardcoded expected string. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
